question: How does the picture change if you compare over 20 years instead of 100 years (GWP20 vs GWP100)?
summary: The ranking stays the same (CO2, CH4, N2O), but the gap narrows sharply. Methane has a GWP of 82.5 over 20 years against 29.8 over 100, because it traps heat strongly but breaks down in about a decade. Using 2024 emissions as the baseline, methane's contribution rises from about 19% to 39%, while CO2 falls from 75% to 56%. N2O moves from 5.9% to 4.4%, because the total grows when the short-lived gas is weighted more.
